title: Deliver the complete five-lesson educator course and assessed cohort exercise
description: Produce one coherent Markdown course-authoring pack under the accepted assessed-course approach. Include five timed 10-15 minute lesson scripts following one fictional cohort; one observable practice output per lesson; ten scenario questions with answers and explanations; an objective/practice/question matrix; a final cohort exercise and scoring rubric; proposed completion criteria, badge wording and landing copy. Verify every product label and capability on the delivery date and link its evidence, reusing existing approved tutorials/help guidance. A second reviewer must be able to apply the rubric to the worked synthetic exercise. Mark missing live access and unverified steps; do not invent successful tests. The completion threshold and badge authority remain team decisions, with no professional accreditation or hiring promise. Deliver all components together at the standard content rate. No course launch, learner recruitment, badge issuance or publication.

goal.title: Create a free "Zedu Certified Educator" mini-course with a shareable badge by Fri Dec 18
goal.description: A short course (5 lessons, 10-15 minutes each) that teaches educators to run a cohort well on Zedu, ending with a quiz and a badge they can share on LinkedIn. Different from the video series, help centre and quick-start guides: this is a structured course with completion. Done = lesson scripts, quiz questions with answers, badge wording and criteria, and the landing page copy. Claims about features must match the live app.

workstream.title: Make the educator badge prove a completed cohort workflow with five assessed lessons
workstream.description: Use one fictional cohort throughout five 10-15 minute lessons: plan its channel structure; write the welcome and announcements; organise resources and learner questions; prepare a Buzz teaching session; and run a weekly review with human follow-up. Each lesson ends with one observable practice output and two scenario questions, rather than passive video completion. Verify all app labels and capabilities against the current product before scripting; reuse the existing help articles and tutorial work rather than re-create them. Deliver one coherent course-authoring pack: five timed scripts, an objective-to-practice-to-question matrix, ten questions with answers and explanations, a final synthetic cohort exercise and rubric, completion/badge wording, and landing copy. Completion threshold is a proposed team decision, not an invented existing certification. Acceptance: all five lessons fit the time budget; every stated capability has dated evidence; each objective is assessed; a reviewer can score the worked exercise consistently; badge copy states what was completed and promises no professional accreditation or employment outcome. Measure pilot completion, question errors and rubric disagreements only with permissioned real data; use labelled synthetic examples until then. This fills the assessment-design gap absent from the existing generic audit/execution proposal. No badge issuance, public course launch, learner recruitment, account changes or publication.
